v.rationale: All three take the same core approach: a nullable customer_id with a nullOnDelete FK added while FK checks are off, a set-based backfill over primary-key ranges, and a switch to the hasMany relation. The differences that decide the ranking are bugs found by probes and how well the indexes fit the queries. Impl-1 had no bugs in my probes. It pins ALGORITHM and LOCK explicitly on MySQL, has both composite indexes and a stable sort, and its rollback works. It loses points for hand-written driver-branching DDL and a $fillable change where the relation would have been more idiomatic. Impl-2 has the most idiomatic Eloquent, a validated request that still handles ?status= correctly, and the strongest tests. Its down() leaves the composite indexes behind, though, so rollback crashes on SQLite and would leave broken indexes on MySQL, and it orders the FK before the indexes, which wastes DDL work. Impl-3 has the cleanest backfill builder, but it breaks the endpoint: ?status= now returns a 422. It also leaves out the (customer_id, created_at) index that the frequent unfiltered call needs, and uses AFTER, which can force a table rebuild on older MySQL 8 versions. All test suites pass (10, 20 and 16 tests). The probe files were deleted afterwards.
